stories.headline: Tidal to ban AI-generated music from December 9, removing millions of tracks
stories.summary: Tidal will stop accepting fully AI-generated music on December 9 and delete a large catalogue of existing AI tracks, reportedly around 27 to 29 million. It will still allow songs made with AI assistance.
stories.why: Streaming platforms are setting policies on AI-generated content, which affects how teams build detection, labelling, and content moderation pipelines.

sources.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming

stories.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, beating rivals on LiveBench
stories.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Neon is presented as a sign that Google DeepMind is back as a frontier lab. It reportedly outperforms Astra and Fable on LiveBench and cut a TypeScript-to-Rust benchmark's runtime by 48.6%.
stories.why: A new frontier model with reported coding gains may change which models teams evaluate and adopt for development work.

sources.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab

stories.headline: DeepMind uses AI agents to run Gemini experiments, but says self-improvement is distant
stories.summary: Google DeepMind is using AI agents to run some experiments for upcoming Gemini models. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement. DeepMind leaves the agents' internal reasoning untrained so humans can review it.
stories.why: Using agents to run research workloads raises practical questions about oversight, review, and automation of experimentation for engineering teams.

sources.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant

stories.headline: Amazon says attackers' AI agents found and exploited a zero-day with little human help
stories.summary: Amazon reports that hackers used AI agents to find and exploit a zero-day vulnerability with minimal human input. The Cairn AI framework is cited as useful to both defenders and attackers.
stories.why: Autonomous AI exploitation shortens the time defenders have to patch, so security practices and patch cadence need review.

sources.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

stories.headline: Anthropic study finds nearly one in five enterprise AI deployments deliver no business value
stories.summary: An Anthropic study of nearly 300 AI deployments across 58 US companies found that about one in five still produce no business value. The researchers blame heavy review workloads, internal bottlenecks, employee resistance, and outdated company structures rather than the tools themselves.
stories.why: The findings suggest that process, review capacity, and team structure often limit AI returns more than tool skill, which matters to engineering leaders planning rollouts.

sources.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools

stories.headline: Anthropic researcher stands by AI-assisted Riemann proof but retracts parts of the rollout
stories.summary: Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge says he still stands by the math in his AI-assisted proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis. He walks back parts of the announcement, including a claimed 250,000-page length, which he called a joke, and says the published Lean code is poor.
stories.why: It is a useful reminder to verify AI-generated formal proofs and code artifacts before trusting the claims made about them.

sources.title: Anthropic researcher stands by his AI-assisted Riemann proof but owns up to "stupid things" in the rollout
What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?

stories.headline: Java4Shell: Oracle and OpenJDK ship fixes for a HotSpot JVM Base64 flaw
stories.summary: On November 17, Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes for CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption bug in the HotSpot JVM's Base64 decoder, reported by Calif and dubbed Java4Shell. JetBrains is urging users to update its IDEs and related tools.
stories.why: Any team running Java workloads or JVM-based developer tools needs to patch promptly to close a memory corruption flaw.

sources.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability: Update Your JetBrains IDEs, ReSharper, .NET Tools, Toolbox App, and Gateway Now

stories.headline: Active intrusion campaign targets Check Point security management servers
stories.summary: A Hacker News discussion highlights an ongoing intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers, which drew substantial attention from the developer community.
stories.why: Security management servers control firewall policy, so an active campaign against them is a risk for any organisation that relies on Check Point.

sources.title: Active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers

stories.headline: AWS doubles Lambda maximum timeout to 30 minutes in all commercial regions
stories.summary: AWS raised the maximum timeout for on-demand Lambda event functions from 15 to 30 minutes, with no opt-in and no new pricing. AWS also notes the change doubles concurrency at the same request rate and affects SQS and Kafka event source settings.
stories.why: The longer limit changes which workloads fit Lambda, but teams should re-check concurrency and event source timeouts before relying on it.

sources.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
AWS Weekly Roundup: Local Zone in Bogotá, 30-minute Lambda timeout, and more (November 24, 2026)

stories.headline: Rust 1.100 stabilises the never type and core allocator API
stories.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released November 12, stabilises the never type after a decade of work and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and adds an opt-in dependency cooldown setting to Cargo.
stories.why: The Cargo cooldown setting and stable allocator core give library and tooling authors new options for supply chain safety and custom memory management.

sources.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts

stories.headline: OpenAI details Pando, a Git backend built for concurrent coding agents
stories.summary: OpenAI has described Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads while keeping standard Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency, achieved by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.
stories.why: As agents push code in parallel, Git server throughput becomes a bottleneck, and this shows one approach that keeps existing workflows intact.

sources.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando

stories.headline: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after near-24-hour Outlook outage
stories.summary: An Exchange Online and Outlook outage this month took email down for millions of customers for nearly a day. Reuters reports Microsoft responded by declaring an unusual internal "Code Red" after a bug on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers triggered it.
stories.why: It is a reminder that a single fault in shared networking infrastructure can disrupt email for millions, and that incident response and gateway reliability matter for any…

sources.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage

stories.headline: VMware ships third critical patch bundle in a week, with four more critical flaws
stories.summary: VMware released another set of patches with four critical vulnerabilities, including a further unauthorized access flaw in vCenter. It is the third critical patch bundle in roughly a week.
stories.why: Teams running vCenter and other VMware infrastructure need to schedule emergency patching quickly, especially around holiday change freezes.

sources.title: This could mess with Thanksgiving, says VMware as it drops third critical patch bundle in a week

stories.headline: US jury finds Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquits it of racketeering
stories.summary: A federal jury in New York found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, including source code and proprietary technology from several companies. It cleared the company of racketeering charges.
stories.why: The verdict centres on source code theft, which matters to engineering leaders thinking about IP protection and the legal risks of vendor and employee code handling.

sources.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
Jury finds Huawei stole US tech, laundered money, and broke sanctions
Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, US jury rules

stories.headline: Nvidia shares fall 7% as scrutiny grows over Jensen Huang's reinstatement
stories.summary: Nvidia's share price dropped 7% as lawmakers pressed the US attorney general about an investigation and about President Trump's involvement in Jensen Huang's reinstatement. Trump has reportedly said a pardon for Huang is 'an option'.
stories.why: Government scrutiny of a dominant chip supplier could affect GPU availability, pricing and export-compliance obligations for teams that depend on it.

sources.title: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is ‘an option’

stories.headline: New paper claims matrix multiplication can be done in Θ(n^2.25) operations
stories.summary: A paper widely shared among developers reports a matrix multiplication complexity of Θ(n^2.25). It drew a large discussion on Hacker News.
stories.why: Improvements to matrix multiplication bounds can eventually influence the algorithms behind numerical libraries and machine learning workloads, though practical gains usually…

sources.title: Matrix Multiplication is Θ(n^2.25) [pdf]

stories.headline: Claude-BugHunter skill bundle tops GitHub Trending with 1,800+ stars in a day
stories.summary: A Python repo offering a Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work gained about 1,800 stars today. It includes 84 skills, 15 slash commands and 681 disclosed-report patterns. Star counts show interest, not proven results.
stories.why: It shows strong developer demand for AI agents that automate security research, which teams may need to evaluate for both defence and misuse.

sources.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 84 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerabilit

stories.headline: CLI-Anything pitches agent-native command lines for all software
stories.summary: The HKUDS project CLI-Anything, which aims to make any software usable by AI agents through a command-line layer, added about 1,070 stars today. It also points to a CLI-Hub. The approach is still early and the claims are not yet independently proven.
stories.why: If agents can drive existing tools through CLIs, teams may need to rethink how internal tools are exposed and secured.

sources.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

stories.headline: Superpowers agentic skills framework keeps climbing GitHub Trending
stories.summary: The obra/superpowers repo, which describes itself as an agentic skills framework and software development methodology, gained about 1,000 stars today and has over 320,000 in total. The popularity is clear, but its real-world impact on productivity is not established.
stories.why: Structured methods for coding agents are becoming a common topic for engineering leads deciding how their teams work with AI.

sources.title: obra/superpowers: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

stories.headline: Firecrawl pitches one API for agent search, scraping and 550+ data providers
stories.summary: Firecrawl describes itself as knowledge infrastructure that lets agents search, scrape and access over 550 data providers through a single API. It gained about 990 stars today and has around 209,000 in total. The claims are the project's own.
stories.why: Agents depend on reliable data access, so teams are weighing whether to buy a managed layer or build their own pipelines.

sources.title: firecrawl/firecrawl: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

stories.headline: minimind claims a 64M-parameter LLM can be trained from scratch in two hours
stories.summary: The minimind repo, with bilingual docs, promises to train a 64-million-parameter language model from scratch in about two hours. It added roughly 730 stars today. This is a small educational-scale demo, not a comparison with production models.
stories.why: It lowers the perceived cost of learning how LLMs are built, which can help engineers understand model training without large budgets.

sources.title: jingyaogong/minimind: 🧠 两小时从 0 训出你的 64M 大模型。Train your own 64M LLM from scratch in 2 hours.

stories.headline: Less experienced developers place more trust in AI, eroding code ownership
stories.summary: LeadDev reports that code ownership is eroding because less experienced developers tend to trust AI output more. The piece treats this as a shift in how teams take responsibility for code.
stories.why: Leads need to decide how review and accountability work when AI-written code is merged by people who may not fully understand it.

sources.title: Code ownership is eroding

stories.headline: JetBrains CEO gives manual code review two years
stories.summary: LeadDev reports that JetBrains' CEO predicts manual code review will end within about two years. The claim points to AI taking over review work.
stories.why: Engineering managers will need to plan review processes, tooling and skill development around a possible move away from manual review.

sources.title: The end of manual code review?

stories.headline: Will Larson merges 170 PRs in a seven-day window
stories.summary: Will Larson describes shipping over 100 pull requests to production in one week, reaching 115 in the week of November 9. His highest seven-day stretch reached 170 merged PRs.
stories.why: The account gives leaders a concrete example of very high delivery throughput and what it takes to reach it, which is useful when setting team output expectations.

sources.title: Shipping 100+ PRs to production in a week

stories.headline: Cannabis users develop psychosis about 2.5 years earlier, with the gap widening with age
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 149 studies found cannabis users developed psychosis on average 2.5 years earlier than non-users. Among adults 30 and older, the gap grew to more than six years, and researchers warn the risks may build up over time.
stories.why: Adds weight to evidence on cannabis and mental health, relevant to leaders setting wellbeing and substance policies for their teams.

sources.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

stories.headline: Researchers identify 'circadian depression', a subtype tied to the body's internal clock
stories.summary: Researchers describe a new depression subtype linked to the body's internal clock, which they say may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression. It is associated with night-owl tendencies, excess sleep and persistent exhaustion, and common antidepressants may work poorly for it.
stories.why: Links sleep timing to a depression type that may need different treatment, relevant to people on shift-heavy or on-call schedules.

sources.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

stories.headline: Problematic smartphone use predicts attention problems rebounding in late adolescence
stories.summary: A study tracking thousands of teenagers found attention symptoms tend to fall in early adolescence and then rebound as adulthood approaches. Struggling to control smartphone use reliably predicted worse behavioural problems over time.
stories.why: Relevant to teams building notification-heavy products and to leaders thinking about device norms for young staff and interns.

sources.title: Problematic smartphone use predicts a rebound in attention issues during late adolescence

stories.headline: Childhood emotional abuse linked to adult mental illness more strongly than physical abuse
stories.summary: A Psychological Bulletin analysis of 104 studies found childhood emotional abuse is linked to adult mental illness more strongly than physical or sexual abuse. Emotional harm is often dismissed because it leaves no visible marks.
stories.why: Highlights how the emotional climate people grow up in shapes later mental health, a useful frame for leaders building psychologically safe teams.

sources.title: Childhood emotional abuse linked to adult mental health struggles more strongly than physical or sexual abuse

stories.headline: Lenders grow pickier as AI borrowing surges, raising doubts over Anthropic debt
stories.summary: Lenders are becoming more selective about corporate bonds as AI companies borrow heavily. Big Tech may find it harder to fund the AI build-out, and there are doubts about whether Anthropic's debt would be rated as junk.
stories.why: Access to debt and its cost can determine how fast AI providers and their cloud customers can expand compute capacity.

sources.title: Anthropic faces junk-debt doubts as AI borrowing surges
AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze

stories.headline: Dell's quarterly sales more than double on AI server demand; $25B buyback approved
stories.summary: Dell beat its third-quarter earnings expectations, with overall sales more than doubling year on year on AI server demand. The company also authorized a $25 billion share buyback.
stories.why: Strong AI server demand signals that infrastructure spending is still growing, which matters for teams planning hardware and cloud capacity.

sources.title: Dell earnings beat on AI strength, company authorizes $25 billion buyback
Dell in spotlight as Wall Street reacts to Q3 results, guidance analyst

stories.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU
stories.summary: The US has proposed new levies on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU, aimed at trade practices it considers unfair or burdensome. The plan follows a Supreme Court ruling earlier this year that struck down broader Trump tariffs.
stories.why: Tariffs can raise the cost of servers, devices and components, and may force changes to hardware sourcing and supply chains.

sources.title: U.S. proposes fresh tariffs on China, others as Trump doubles down on his favorite trade weapon
U.S. proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU

stories.headline: Preferred US inflation gauge rises to 3.8% in October; December rate hike seen likely
stories.summary: The Fed's preferred inflation measure reportedly accelerated to 3.8% in October, and a rate hike in December is now considered likely. Higher borrowing costs would arrive heading into the holiday season.
stories.why: Higher rates raise the cost of capital for startups and can slow hiring and funding decisions for engineering teams.

sources.title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge accelerated to 3.8% in October, likely sealing rate hike
